name: Ken Calloway
life: “I still remember counting the family change into a cabbage basket.” On Thursday, near the foot of Harbor Viaduct, Ken pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I was ashamed my family lived on leftovers. The visiting cook asked if she could come to our house.
appearance: Ken has heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw. Look for a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a striped cotton shirt with a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric. In conversation Ken holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Ken admires skill and distrusts the idea that skill gives anyone permission to be rude. Ken learns fastest from somebody willing to show how they made a mistake.
agenda: To invite the visiting cook for a family supper.
family: Ivy Burke is Ken’s cousin raised in the same household. Ken saves a place. Ivy chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The third bedroom*, Ivy says, “I want to stay their carer. Our spare room pays the mortgage with a lodger in it.”
connections: Ashley Lang. A leftover meal brings the visiting cook and a family language into one kitchen.

reactions.situation: Someone in the soup line cannot eat one ingredient
reactions.response: Ken asks the cook to identify the ingredients before offering a separate bowl.

reactions.situation: A diner goes silent in the middle of a noisy family celebration
reactions.response: Ken takes a small plate to the quieter end of the table and saves the seat beside it.
